thread:
incidents-bot: PAGER: HIGH - potential cross-customer routing mismatch detected for Dedicated pool eu-west-2. Paging @eva (on-call) and @rajiv. Auto-triage suggests anomalous route_to_customer for pool-id: dp-44b7

incidents-bot: Detection summary: 7 requests in last 5m routed to dp-44b7 with unexpected tenant headers; high confidence: 0.87. Severity recommended: P1 if confirmed. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/1794523345

eva (on-call): On it. give me a quick ETA, @rajiv?

rajiv (infra): ETA 10m. Pulling routing table diffs now. Suspect a recent rollout of route-mapper 2.3.1 on dp-44b7.

jules (eng-runtime): Noted. dp-44b7 runs runtime v5.7 + kernel-opt. If routing layer mislabels tenant tags we could see cross-tenant KV cache hits. We should check prefix_cache and grpc-mux logs.

eva (on-call): Sophie, can you flag affected customer(s) so CS is ready if this is confirmed? Which customers are on that pool?

sophie (customer-success): dp-44b7 assigned to Cust-311 (enterprise), Cust-842 (sandbox), and a couple of internal test namespaces. I'll prep a holding message to send if we confirm exposure.

rajiv (infra): Pasting initial checks:
```
# on router-3
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/route-mapper status dp-44b7 --diff  --since 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
--output=short
```
Result: route-mapper config changed 2026-03-12T04:22:18Z by deploy-bot, config key mismatch: tenant-shard -> tenant-label.

rajiv (infra): Also grep'd logs: `grep "unexpected tenant" /var/log/router-3/route-mapper.log | tail -n 50` -> 7 matching entries. Sample:
```
[2026-03-15T11:05:23Z] INFO route-mapper: resolved request -> tenant-label=cust-311, route_to=dp-44b7, observed-tenant-header=cust-842
```

jules (eng-runtime): That looks like header mixup at the ingress normalization layer. Could be a change in header canonicalization that was deployed with route-mapper 2.3.1. If requests carry legacy header X-Redwood-Tenant vs X-Rdw-Tenant we map wrong.

eva (on-call): Immediate mitigation: 1) Quarantine dp-44b7 from onboarding new requests (set drain=true) 2) Apply a temporary ACL on router-3 to reject requests where observed-tenant-header != tenant-label 3) Notify affected customers. I'll run 1 and 2 now.

eva (on-call): `./runbook quarantine-pool --pool dp-44b7 --reason "suspected cross-tenant routing"`

ops-runbook-bot: ACTIONED quarantine: dp-44b7 set to DRAINING by eva at 2026-03-15T11:12:10Z. Active connections allowed to finish, new sessions rejected.

rajiv (infra): Applied temp ACL on router-3:
```
sudo iptables -I INPUT -m string --algo bm --string "X-Rdw-Tenant:" -j ACCEPT
# fallback drop for mismatched header condition handled at app layer (nginx lua script updated)
```

jules (eng-runtime): I'm rolling a hotfix to ingress-normalizer to treat both header variants consistently and log the canonical tenant header. Patch: v2.3.2 hotfix with explicit header precedence and additional telemetry. Preparing canary on router-7 first.

sophie (customer-success): Drafting notification to Cust-311 and Cust-842. Asking for permission to provide a private postmortem if they request. Cust-311 SLA: enterprise, needs immediate escalation.

eva (on-call): Good. @jules prioritize canary then cluster rollout if green within 10m. Keep dp-44b7 quarantined until we verify no cross-tenant access in logs.

jules (eng-runtime): Canary applied to router-7 at 11:22Z. Early logs show no new mismatches. Telemetry: tenant_resolution_errors dropped to 0 over 3m. Pushing v2.3.2 to router-3 now.

rajiv (infra): Applying patch to router-3 now, backing up current config `cp /etc/route-mapper/conf.yaml /tmp/conf.yaml.bak`.

incidents-bot: NOTE: customer-impact flag set -> potential data exposure until quarantined. Recommend legal & security loop-in.

eva (on-call): Paging security and legal via the incident channel. @sophie keep Cust-311 updated that we're actively mitigating and quarantine is in place.

sophie (customer-success): Sent holding note to Cust-311 (internal ticket #CS-4521). Message: "We detected anomalous routing behavior affecting a dedicated capacity pool assigned to your org and a sandbox tenant. We have quarantined the pool and are rolling a fix. No evidence yet of persisted cross-tenant storage access, but we're investigating. We'll follow up with findings and next steps."

jules (eng-runtime): Patch complete on router-3 at 11:34Z. Replayed the 7 suspicious requests against a safe proxy -> no sensitive response observed (responses were truncated/noise). Still doing full KV prefix audit.

rajiv (infra): Running KV cache audit: `python3 tools/kv_audit.py --pool dp-44b7 --since 2026-03-15T10:30:00Z --match-tenant-headers`
Output (summary): 0 confirmed cross-tenant key reads. 3 ambiguous cache hits where keys lacked tenant-prefixed namespace; those keys map to internal-test namespaces, not enterprise customer data.

eva (on-call): That's encouraging. What's left for closure?

jules (eng-runtime): Steps to close: 1) Verify no persisted cross-tenant writes (KV store and logs) 2) Rotate any ephemeral service tokens that could've been leaked (none found) 3) Fully restore dp-44b7 from drained state after a controlled traffic soak 4) Postmortem with root cause and rollout prevention.

rajiv (infra): KV write check in progress. No suspicious write operations between 10:30-11:40Z.

ops-runbook-bot: NOTE: Scheduled on-call handoff at 2026-03-15T12:00Z. @eva to handoff to next on-call: @rajiv (infra).

eva (on-call): I'll handoff after I verify KV audit completes and CS has sent cust updates. If we still see ambiguous items, we won't unquarantine.

sophie (customer-success): Cust-311 ack'd receipt and appreciates the proactive approach. Requested a short call once we have the full audit. I've scheduled a 30m slot for 13:00 UTC.

jules (eng-runtime): Final KV write check done: no enterprise customer writes observed. Ambiguous keys belong to internal-test namespace, will be purged. I'm running a safe purge and will re-run validation.

rajiv (infra): Purge complete at 11:56Z. Re-run of audit confirms 0 cross-tenant reads/writes.

ops-runbook-bot: ACTIONED unquarantine: dp-44b7 flagged for controlled rejoin at 12:05Z pending soak.

eva (on-call): Rejoin completed at 12:10Z. Monitoring realtime metrics; tenant-mismatch metric remains at baseline.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated). Severity downgraded to P3 pending postmortem.

sophie (customer-success): Sent update to Cust-311: mitigation complete, no evidence of cross-tenant data exposure, scope limited to routing header normalization bug. Offered postmortem and mitigation timeline. They accepted a brief call.

jules (eng-runtime): Root cause: route-mapper 2.3.1 changed header canonicalization order; ingress-normalizer expected `X-Rdw-Tenant` but some upstream proxies sent `X-Redwood-Tenant`. Hotfix reconciled both and added strict validation. Rollout policy updated to include tenant-mismatch alerting threshold.

eva (on-call): Good work. Postmortem to include timeline, systems/owners, remediation (hotfix + alerting + pre-deploy config diff check), and customer communication artifacts. Assigning postmortem owner: @jules.

jules (eng-runtime): I'll own the postmortem. Tentative draft by EOD.

sophie (customer-success): I'll prepare the customer-facing postmortem and coordinate legal review if required.

eva (on-call): Closing handoff to @rajiv who will be on-call for the next slot. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

rajiv (infra): Acknowledged. Logged incident under INC-2026-0315-01 and linked relevant runbooks.

incidents-bot: Thread archived.
